staged_source_snapshot.description: This host-side `_work` checkout is the staged vulnerable source snapshot for the sample. The live ARVO workspace container exposes the same tree at `/src/librawspeed`; Stage 02 grounded the trace in this staged vulnerable tree and the saved ASan report only.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 5296 (rawspeed): Container-overflow READ 8. Crash State: rawspeed::Spline<unsigned short, void>::prepare -> rawspeed::Spline<unsigned short, void>::Spline -> rawspeed::IiqDecoder::CorrectQuadrantMultipliersCombined. Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.normalized: The staged 954-byte witness is accepted by the IIQ/TIFF path and reaches `rawspeed::IiqDecoder::CorrectQuadrantMultipliersCombined()`, which reads seven shared x-coordinates plus quadrant y multipliers from correction-metadata tag `0x431` and builds a 9-point control-point vector for a `Spline<>`. In `rawspeed::Spline<unsigned short, void>::Spline`, that vector yields `num_coords = 9` and `num_segments = 8`, and `segments.resize(num_coords)` allocates nine logical `Segment` elements. `prepare()` then executes `segments.pop_back()`, shrinking the vector's logical size to 8, but the reverse loop still unconditionally binds `Segment& sn = segments[i + 1]`. On the first iteration `i == 7`, so `sn` aliases `segments[8]`, one past the vector's logical end. The next line reads `sn.c`, and AddressSanitizer reports the saved container-overflow READ of size 8 at `src/librawspeed/common/Spline.h:97`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the traced vulnerable path that materializes the attacker-controlled correction-metadata blob into a `ByteStream` later consumed by the quadrant-multiplier parser.
source.value_from: The staged 954-byte IIQ/TIFF witness carries a top-level directory entry with tag `0x110`; its file-supplied offset `data` is used here to create the correction-metadata stream that later reaches `CorrectPhaseOneC()` and `CorrectQuadrantMultipliersCombined()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. This statement dereferences `sn.c` after `sn` has already been bound to `segments[i + 1]` beyond the vector's logical end.
sink.note: On the first reverse-loop iteration `i == 7`, `sn` refers to the popped `segments[8]` element. Reading `sn.c` produces the saved container-overflow READ of size 8 at `Spline.h:97:31`.

root_cause.description: After `segments.pop_back()` shrinks the vector to `num_segments` elements, this line still derives the next segment as `segments[i + 1]` for every reverse-loop iteration. On the first iteration `i + 1` equals the vector size, so `sn` becomes a one-past-end reference.
root_cause.note: The missing obligation is a terminal-segment special case or an equivalent bounds-preserving representation after the pop. The staged patch does not change this line or the surrounding reverse-loop logic.

tainted_value_origin.description: This call extracts the exact correction-metadata substream that supplies the spline x/y control-point data.
tainted_value_origin.note: The inner correction directory entry tagged `0x431` provides the `offset,len` pair for the quadrant-multipliers blob. That blob is the direct source of the seven shared x-coordinates and four sets of y multipliers consumed by `CorrectQuadrantMultipliersCombined()`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is accepted past TIFF parsing and IIQ decoder selection, so `IiqDecoder::decodeRawInternal()` runs. The later width/height and split-coordinate checks at lines 182-187 also pass, allowing the correction-metadata loop to reach tag `0x110` and then call `CorrectPhaseOneC()`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, and no `trace_feedback.json` was staged, so Stage 02 did not instrument or re-run the target beyond the saved Stage 01 vulnerable reproduction.

Stage 01 preserved only the vulnerable ASan run. There is no staged fixed-build execution or secondary detector trace for this sample, so `cross_tool_confirmed` remains `false` and `patch_resolves` is grounded only by source inspection of `patch.diff`.

The staged `patch.diff` edits only `Spline::calculateCurve()` clamping logic. It does not touch `prepare()`, `segments.pop_back()`, or the `segments[i + 1]` access at `src/librawspeed/common/Spline.h:95-97`, so it does not resolve the reproduced container-overflow path.

fine_trace.note: Source. When the top-level IIQ entry loop encounters tag `0x110`, this statement materializes the attacker-controlled correction-metadata blob as a `ByteStream` starting at the file-supplied offset `data`. The later call at line 209 proves the witness assigned a non-empty stream here.

Because step 1 produced a non-empty stream and `iiq.quadrantMultipliers` is enabled by default, the decoder enters `CorrectPhaseOneC()` with the attacker-controlled correction metadata and the previously validated split coordinates.

Inside the correction-metadata directory, the current 12-byte entry materializes its dispatch tag and the byte range of the pointed payload. On the crashing path this entry is the quadrant-multipliers record `tag == 0x431`.
The `0x431` case extracts the exact substream at `offset,len` and passes it to `CorrectQuadrantMultipliersCombined()`. This blob is the direct source of the spline x/y control-point data.

The function reads seven attacker-controlled x coordinates from step 4's substream and completes the shared x-axis with fixed endpoints `0` and `65535`, producing the nine x positions used for every quadrant curve.
Reachability guard. The witness's x coordinates are strictly increasing, so this exception path is not taken and spline control points continue to be built.

On the first quadrant loop iteration, seven attacker-controlled y multipliers are read and scaled against step 5's x coordinates. Because each `y_coord <= 65535`, the code keeps appending points and ends with a 9-point `control_points[0][0]` vector: fixed `(0,0)` and `(65535,65535)` endpoints plus seven interior points.

The first `Spline<>` constructor sees step 7's nine control points, so it derives `num_coords = 9` and `num_segments = 8`. Those counts drive both the later vector extent and the reverse-loop index that oversteps it.

Allocation context. Using step 8's `num_coords == 9`, the constructor allocates `segments` with nine logical `Segment` elements. Lines 138-140 then populate those slots from the control points before `prepare()` runs.

After using the last slot as temporary storage for the final control point, `prepare()` drops that trailing element. The vector's logical size becomes `num_segments == 8`, so valid indices are now `0..7` even though the old slot 8 still lies inside the same allocation.

Root cause. The reverse loop starts at `i = num_segments - 1 == 7`, but after step 10 the vector size is also 8. There is no terminal-segment special case and no `i + 1 < segments.size()` guard, so `sn` is bound to `segments[8]`, one past the logical end.

Sink. Step 11's out-of-range `sn` reference is dereferenced here. Reading `sn.c` touches the popped `segments[8]` slot's container redzone and AddressSanitizer reports the saved 8-byte container-overflow READ at `Spline.h:97:31`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch only clamps `Spline::calculateCurve()` output and does not modify `prepare()`, `segments.pop_back()`, or the post-pop `segments[i + 1]` read at `src/librawspeed/common/Spline.h:95-97`, so it does not resolve the reproduced container-overflow.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context names the same `segments.resize(num_coords)` vector whose logical size step 10 shrinks before step 11 derives `segments[i + 1]`; the logical bug is the later post-pop access, not the allocation itself.

format.name: Phase One IIQ/TIFF raw
format.contract: A crafted IIQ/TIFF raw that is accepted by `TiffParser` and `IiqDecoder`, carries a non-empty top-level correction-metadata tag `0x110` whose inner directory contains tag `0x431`, and supplies strictly increasing shared x-coordinates plus y multipliers that satisfy the existing `y_coord <= 65535` guard, so `CorrectQuadrantMultipliersCombined()` constructs the 9-point `Spline` that deterministically hits the post-`pop_back()` `segments[i + 1]` read.
